correctness.rationale: For Q with vertices (0,0),(-2,-1),(-3,-2),(-2,-3),(-1,-2), primitive cyclic edge vectors d0..d4 as displayed, Altmann miniversal Minkowski equations G_k=sum d_j t_j^k after translation apply to this isolated toric Gorenstein cone. Solving G1 gives t=(u,v,0,3u+v,-u). Independent symbolic expansion verifies G2=(8u^2+6uv,10u^2+6uv), generating ideal exactly (u^2,uv) in characteristic zero. For every k>=2 modulo that ideal, u^k=(-u)^k=0 and (v+3u)^k=v^k, so only d1v^k+d3v^k=0; hence all higher equations are redundant, not merely the checked degrees through 20. Completion gives C[[u,v]]/(u^2,uv). u is a nonzero square-zero element killed by maximal ideal (u,v), so its support is an embedded associated point while the generic reduced line is smooth. The result depends on Altmann’s isolated-versal theorem, not a direct global Calabi-Yau deformation computation.
